groups.name: shadcn variables
groups.note: The names every shadcn component reads.

groups.name: Lede extras
groups.note: Surfaces, fills, glass and status beyond shadcn’s set.

tokens.name: primary
tokens.usage: shadcn `--primary`. The one interactive hue: filled buttons, links, selection, switch-on, the selected tab. Text in `primary` reads on `background`, `background-grouped`, `card` and `muted` in every theme. Rebrand by overriding this one token, or with ThemeProvider’s `accent`.

tokens.name: primary-foreground
tokens.usage: shadcn `--primary-foreground`. Text and glyphs on a `primary` fill. White in light themes, near-black in dark and black in dark-hc, where `primary` lightens. Every `preset-*` reaches 4.5:1 against it (7:1 in -hc).

tokens.name: preset-blue
tokens.usage: Accent preset `blue`. Pass `accent="blue"` to ThemeProvider to make it `primary`. Tuned per theme so `primary-foreground` text and accent-on-surface text both pass.

tokens.name: preset-indigo
tokens.usage: Accent preset `indigo`. Pass `accent="indigo"` to ThemeProvider to make it `primary`. Tuned per theme so `primary-foreground` text and accent-on-surface text both pass.

tokens.name: preset-teal
tokens.usage: Accent preset `teal`. Pass `accent="teal"` to ThemeProvider to make it `primary`. Tuned per theme so `primary-foreground` text and accent-on-surface text both pass.

tokens.name: preset-green
tokens.usage: Accent preset `green`. Pass `accent="green"` to ThemeProvider to make it `primary`. Tuned per theme so `primary-foreground` text and accent-on-surface text both pass.

tokens.name: preset-orange
tokens.usage: Accent preset `orange`. Pass `accent="orange"` to ThemeProvider to make it `primary`. Tuned per theme so `primary-foreground` text and accent-on-surface text both pass.

tokens.name: preset-pink
tokens.usage: Accent preset `pink`. Pass `accent="pink"` to ThemeProvider to make it `primary`. Tuned per theme so `primary-foreground` text and accent-on-surface text both pass.

tokens.name: preset-graphite
tokens.usage: Accent preset `graphite`. Pass `accent="graphite"` to ThemeProvider to make it `primary`. Tuned per theme so `primary-foreground` text and accent-on-surface text both pass. Also the fill of a neutral swipe action.

tokens.name: background
tokens.usage: shadcn `--background`. Page background for content-led screens (media, documents, canvases).

tokens.name: foreground
tokens.usage: shadcn `--foreground`. Primary text and glyphs on every surface: `background`, `background-grouped`, `card`, `muted`, `secondary`, `glass-tint`.

tokens.name: background-grouped
tokens.usage: Lede extra. Background behind grouped content: settings, forms, ListGroup, Disclosure and Card stacks.

tokens.name: card
tokens.usage: shadcn `--card`. Raised surfaces on `background-grouped`, such as Card, ListGroup, Disclosure, SummaryCard, Table, FormSection, an open message and WorkbenchShell’s center panel.

tokens.name: card-foreground
tokens.usage: shadcn `--card-foreground`. Text on `card`.

tokens.name: popover
tokens.usage: shadcn `--popover`. Menus, such as the ••• menu of a ListRow or a DataTable row.

tokens.name: popover-foreground
tokens.usage: shadcn `--popover-foreground`. Text on `popover`.

tokens.name: muted
tokens.usage: shadcn `--muted`. A second raised step nested inside `card`: a Disclosure or a list inside a Disclosure, and a `muted` Card.

tokens.name: muted-foreground
tokens.usage: shadcn `--muted-foreground`. Secondary text: summaries, subtitles, hints, placeholders, trailing values. 4.5:1 (7:1 in -hc) on page surfaces, rows and gray fills, and on glass in -hc. On glass in light and dark it isn’t held, since content of any color can show behind. As an icon it holds 3:1 at `opacity-hint` and `opacity-resting`.

tokens.name: foreground-disabled
tokens.usage: Lede extra. A disabled control’s label and text, on a page surface or `fill-control`, which WCAG 1.4.3 exempts from contrast. Text a person needs to read uses `foreground` or `muted-foreground`.

tokens.name: secondary
tokens.usage: shadcn `--secondary`. Gray (secondary) button fill.

tokens.name: secondary-foreground
tokens.usage: shadcn `--secondary-foreground`. Text on `secondary`.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: shadcn `--accent`. The quiet highlight under a hovered or highlighted item: menu items, sidebar links, ••• buttons and AccentPicker options. The brand hue is `primary`.

tokens.name: accent-foreground
tokens.usage: shadcn `--accent-foreground`. Text on `accent`.

tokens.name: fill-control
tokens.usage: Lede extra. Resting fill of gray buttons (through `secondary`), text fields, selects, segmented-control tracks, step marks, skeletons and an inbox thread’s count. Also the fill of a pressed, hovered or current row, a pressed heading that opens a section, a pressed SummaryCard and a hovered or toggled-on toolbar button.

tokens.name: fill-control-strong
tokens.usage: Lede extra. Switch off-track and hovered gray buttons.

tokens.name: fill-selected
tokens.usage: Lede extra. The selected segment of a SegmentedControl, on `fill-control`. `foreground` reads on it.

tokens.name: fill-knob
tokens.usage: Lede extra. Switch knob. White in every theme, on `primary` or `fill-control-strong`.

tokens.name: border
tokens.usage: shadcn `--border`. Decorative hairlines between rows and sections. In -hc themes it becomes a 3:1 rule.

tokens.name: input
tokens.usage: shadcn `--input`. The edge of a control whose fill alone doesn’t show a boundary. In every theme: a text field, a table select, a switch’s off track and the selected segment. In -hc also every other control fill, and cards, list groups, disclosures, menus, tables, avatars and block edges such as the sidebar’s and a summary card’s. 3:1 on every page surface and on a segmented control’s track. A checkbox’s edge is `muted-foreground`, and `foreground` in -hc.

tokens.name: ring
tokens.usage: shadcn `--ring`. Keyboard focus ring, `stroke-ring` wide at `stroke-ring-offset`. Follows `primary`, so it re-themes too. 3:1 on page surfaces, rows and glass over any content, in every theme and accent.

tokens.name: destructive
tokens.usage: shadcn `--destructive`. Errors and destructive actions. As text on every surface but glass in light and dark, where `--ld-destructive-on-tint` reads, or as a fill under `destructive-foreground`. Always with a word or icon.

tokens.name: destructive-foreground
tokens.usage: Text on a `destructive` fill: white in light themes, near-black in dark and black in dark-hc.

tokens.name: success
tokens.usage: Lede extra. Success and completion, as text on every surface but glass in light and dark. Always with a word or icon.

tokens.name: warning
tokens.usage: Lede extra. Warnings, as text on every surface but glass in light and dark. Always with a word or icon.

tokens.name: glass-tint
tokens.usage: Lede extra. Fill of the glass material (GlassBar, GlassToolbar, a glass Button or Card), blurred by `blur-regular`. Opaque in -hc. Over content of any color, `foreground`, `--ld-destructive-on-tint` and `ring` read on it; secondary and status colors don’t in light and dark.

tokens.name: glass-stroke
tokens.usage: Lede extra. Hairline outline of glass and menus, which separates them from content of any color. In -hc it’s 1px wide and 9:1 against `glass-tint`, so the two give 3:1 against anything behind.

tokens.name: glass-highlight
tokens.usage: Lede extra. Inner top-edge highlight on glass. Off in -hc.

tokens.name: scrim
tokens.usage: Lede extra. For dimming content behind a modal sheet or dialog. Lede’s CSS doesn’t paint it: Lede has no modal overlay, and menus don’t dim the page.

type.note: Sizes, line heights and letter spacing are in rem, so text follows the browser’s text size. Each style is also three properties, `--text-<style>-size`, `-line-height` and `-weight`, and a fourth, `-letter-spacing`, if it sets letter spacing. The `.text-*` classes and the components read them. Keyed by `options`, like `size`. No style differs by density.

families.sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, system-ui, "Segoe UI", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
families.mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace

styles.name: large-title
styles.usage: A screen’s one title, which PageHeader sets. SummaryCard’s figure takes its size too.

styles.name: title-1
styles.usage: Section openers in content-led layouts. SummaryCard’s figure takes its size under `breakpoint-reflow`.

styles.name: title-2
styles.usage: Titles of a card or pane, such as an open message’s subject. A large Avatar’s initials take its size.

styles.name: title-3
styles.usage: Sub-sections, and an empty state’s title. AppShell’s brand takes its size.

styles.name: headline
styles.usage: Emphasized body: a Disclosure’s title, a table’s caption and a large Button’s label.

styles.name: body
styles.usage: Default reading text and list-row titles.
styles.sample: Content comes first; the interface steps back.

styles.name: subheadline
styles.usage: Row subtitles, field labels, button labels at regular size.

styles.name: footnote
styles.usage: ListGroup headers and footers, hints under fields.

styles.name: caption-1
styles.usage: Captions under media, timestamps. Lede’s CSS doesn’t use it.

styles.name: caption-2
styles.usage: GlassBar’s tab labels. It is the smallest style, and at the default text size Lede sets no text smaller.

styles.name: numeral
styles.usage: Big glanceable figures: timers, stats, counters. Lede’s CSS doesn’t use it.

styles.name: code
styles.usage: Code, tokens and identifiers. Lede’s CSS doesn’t use it.

weight.note: Font weights for emphasis on a style’s metrics. Each type style carries its own weight too.

tokens.name: weight-regular
tokens.usage: Plain text. Lede’s CSS doesn’t use it.

tokens.name: weight-medium
tokens.usage: Tab-bar, toolbar, sidebar and segment labels.

tokens.name: weight-semibold
tokens.usage: Emphasis: button labels, current items, table headers, titles that lead.

tokens.name: weight-bold
tokens.usage: Display titles and the app’s name.

spacing.note: A 4px grid, with half steps at 2px and 6px. The half steps are for gaps inside one control and between a label and what it labels. In their names `_` stands for the decimal point, so `space-0_5` is half of `space-1`. Keyed by `options`, like `size`. No step differs by density.

tokens.name: space-0_5
tokens.usage: Half step. Gaps between items packed into one bar or control (tab-bar items, sidebar links, a title and its summary), and the segmented control’s inset.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Icon-to-label gap, tight inline gaps.

tokens.name: space-1_5
tokens.usage: Step and a half. Between a label and what it labels: a field’s label and input, a list’s header or footer and its group, a legend and its form, a swatch and its name, a glyph and its word (a status dot, the back link’s chevron). Also a menu’s inset, the padding above and below a menu item with a reason and how far inside the data table’s ••• its forced-colors outline sits.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Gap between related controls; the concentric inset step.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Text-field and small-button padding.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Default padding: list rows, cards, screen gutters on phones.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Large-button padding.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Gap between grouped sections.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Gap between major regions.

tokens.name: space-12
tokens.usage: The largest step: the room around an empty state and at the foot of AppShell’s page.

radius.note: Capsules and circles aside, every corner derives from one seed, `--radius` (shadcn’s), and one step, `--radius-step`. The chain: `--radius-xl` = radius + step, `--radius-lg` = radius, `--radius-md` = radius − step, `--radius-sm` = radius − 1.5 steps, `--radius-xs` = radius − 2 steps, none under a quarter step. In `soft` they are 30, 22, 14, 10 and 6px. Change `radius` and the chain follows. A capsule is `--radius-capsule`: fully round in `soft` and `crisp`, 6px in `square`. Dots, swatches and step marks are circles in every shape. The step equals `space-2`, the inset between nested containers, so nested corners stay concentric. It is a token of its own, so a density can change spacing without moving corners. Values are keyed by `options`, which are ThemeProvider’s `shape` values, the first being the default.

tokens.name: radius
tokens.usage: shadcn `--radius`, which is `--radius-lg`: ListGroup, Disclosure, Card. The rest of the chain derives from it.

tokens.name: radius-capsule
tokens.usage: Buttons, GlassBar, SegmentedControl, Switch: anything a finger presses is a capsule, except in `square`.

tokens.name: radius-step
tokens.usage: The step between radii in the chain, and the inset at which nested corners stay concentric.

stroke.note: Line widths and offsets beyond hairlines. A 0.5px or 1px line needs no token.

tokens.name: stroke-ring
tokens.usage: Keyboard focus ring width and the state rings drawn at its weight: an invalid field, a checkbox’s edge in -hc, a quote’s bar, an accent swatch’s ring and the data table’s error edge in forced colors.

tokens.name: stroke-ring-offset
tokens.usage: Gap between a control and its focus ring, and between an accent swatch and its ring.

tokens.name: stroke-control
tokens.usage: A control’s own edge where it carries meaning: the Checkbox box, the data table’s error panel.

tokens.name: stroke-marker
tokens.usage: The bar that marks the current or selected item where a fill can’t (-hc, forced colors), and a divider’s grip.

tokens.name: stroke-underline-offset
tokens.usage: Gap under a link’s underline in a table row.

shadow.note: Shadows say that something floats above content. Lede puts them only on glass, menus and raised controls.

tokens.name: shadow-float
tokens.usage: Glass and menus floating over content: GlassBar, GlassToolbar, the ••• menu and a glass Button or Card.

tokens.name: shadow-raised
tokens.usage: The raised item in a group: a SegmentedControl’s selected segment, and the current item of a GlassBar or of AppShell’s sidebar.

tokens.name: shadow-knob
tokens.usage: Switch knob. Its first shadow is a 1px edge, which scripts/check-contrast.mjs reads: the knob shows against its track by its fill or this edge, at 3:1.

blur.note: Backdrop blur radii for glass, the translucent material of GlassBar, GlassToolbar and a glass Button or Card, which blurs what’s behind it. Each blur goes with `blur-saturation`.

tokens.name: blur-thin
tokens.usage: A lighter blur, for small glass over simple content. Lede’s own glass uses `blur-regular`.

tokens.name: blur-regular
tokens.usage: Every glass surface in Lede: GlassBar, GlassToolbar, a glass Button or Card.

tokens.name: blur-thick
tokens.usage: A heavier blur, for glass over busy media. Lede’s own glass uses `blur-regular`.

tokens.name: blur-saturation
tokens.usage: The saturation boost that goes with every glass blur.

size.note: Control heights, glyph sizes, the fixed parts of controls and the largest some labels get. Keyed by `options`, which are ThemeProvider’s `density` values, the first being the default. `touch` is for screens used with a finger: its smallest control is `size-hit-min` tall. Only control heights and the row button differ by density. A button or field’s hit target is its height. List rows and bar items keep `size-hit-min` at every density. Table rows and checkboxes take `size-control-md` + `space-2`, capped at `size-hit-min` and at least `size-hit-absolute-min`.

tokens.name: size-control-sm
tokens.usage: Small buttons and segmented controls (`size="sm"`), and the width of WorkbenchShell’s dividers on a device without a touch screen.

tokens.name: size-control-md
tokens.usage: Default button, text field and segmented control height.

tokens.name: size-control-lg
tokens.usage: Large buttons and text fields (`size="lg"`), and the room AppShell and SelectionBar leave for the floating tab bar.

tokens.name: size-hit-min
tokens.usage: Minimum touch target: list rows, tab items. Pad small controls out to this.

tokens.name: size-hit-absolute-min
tokens.usage: The smallest area a press on any control reaches: 24px (WCAG 2.5.8), and `size-hit-min` in `touch`. A control drawn smaller, such as a small Button, a SegmentedControl’s option or an AppShell footer link, reaches it with a pseudo-element or an input that overhangs its box.

tokens.name: size-leading
tokens.usage: ListRow’s leading slot and what fills it: an icon tile, or an Avatar at its default size.

tokens.name: size-icon
tokens.usage: The Checkbox’s box and the glyphs in toolbar buttons, sidebar links and row menus.

tokens.name: size-icon-lg
tokens.usage: Tab-bar glyphs, and the inbox’s checkbox.

tokens.name: size-icon-inline
tokens.usage: An icon in a line of text, such as a Button’s. In em, so it follows the label’s size.

tokens.name: size-row-button
tokens.usage: A round icon-only button inside a row: ListRow’s •••. In `touch` it’s a hit target on its own; elsewhere a coarse pointer gets a `size-hit-min` hit area around it.

tokens.name: size-chevron
tokens.usage: Height of a disclosure chevron: ListRow, Disclosure, SummaryCard, a collapsible Table.

tokens.name: size-sort-arrow
tokens.usage: Height of a table header’s sort arrows.

tokens.name: size-status-dot
tokens.usage: The dot beside a status word.

tokens.name: size-unread-dot
tokens.usage: The dot that marks an unread row.

tokens.name: size-step-mark
tokens.usage: StepIndicator’s numbered mark.

tokens.name: size-switch-width
tokens.usage: Switch track width.

tokens.name: size-switch-height
tokens.usage: Switch track height.

tokens.name: size-switch-inset
tokens.usage: Gap between the Switch’s knob and its track. The knob is the track’s height less two insets.

tokens.name: size-avatar-lg
tokens.usage: A large Avatar, as at the top of a profile. The default Avatar is `size-leading`.

tokens.name: size-swatch
tokens.usage: AccentPicker’s color swatch.

tokens.name: size-tab-min-width
tokens.usage: The narrowest a tab-bar item gets, unless five share a narrow screen.

tokens.name: size-menu-min-width
tokens.usage: The narrowest a Menu gets.

tokens.name: size-bar-label-max
tokens.usage: The largest a GlassBar label gets, `caption-2` at the default text size, so five places still fit across a phone as text grows. A project with a larger `caption-2` sets this to match.

tokens.name: size-bar-label-line-max
tokens.usage: The tallest a GlassBar label’s line gets, to go with `size-bar-label-max`.

tokens.name: size-row-action-max
tokens.usage: The largest a swipe action’s label gets when the actions at the text size don’t fit the row: `subheadline` at the default text size.

tokens.name: size-row-action-line-max
tokens.usage: The tallest a swipe action label’s line gets in the same case, to go with `size-row-action-max`.

layout.note: Widths and heights of layouts, in the unit each works in. Not keyed.

tokens.name: layout-sidebar-width
tokens.usage: AppShell’s sidebar column on wide screens. SelectionBar starts beside it.

tokens.name: layout-list-min-width
tokens.usage: MasterDetail’s list column, side by side, at its narrowest.

tokens.name: layout-list-max-width
tokens.usage: MasterDetail’s list column, side by side, at its widest.

tokens.name: layout-flow-max-width
tokens.usage: The widest a hero flow gets.

tokens.name: layout-flow-narrow-max-width
tokens.usage: The widest a narrow flow, such as a form, gets.

tokens.name: layout-message-max-width
tokens.usage: The widest an open message gets, side by side.

tokens.name: layout-summary-min-width
tokens.usage: The narrowest a SummaryCard gets in its grid. In rem, so the grid holds fewer columns at larger text sizes.

tokens.name: layout-summary-wide-min-width
tokens.usage: The narrowest a SummaryCard gets in its grid on wide screens. In rem, like `layout-summary-min-width`.

tokens.name: layout-swatch-min-width
tokens.usage: The narrowest an AccentPicker cell gets.

tokens.name: layout-measure-max-width
tokens.usage: The longest line of prose.

tokens.name: layout-measure-short-max-width
tokens.usage: The longest line of a short note, such as an empty state’s.

tokens.name: layout-table-max-height
tokens.usage: The tallest a Table that scrolls sideways gets before it scrolls down too. `--ld-table-max-height` overrides it per table.

opacity.note: How faint a state or a resting mark is.

tokens.name: opacity-disabled
tokens.usage: Lede’s CSS doesn’t use it: a disabled control takes `fill-control` and a `foreground-disabled` label. For a disabled state of your own that dims.

tokens.name: opacity-pressed
tokens.usage: Lede’s CSS doesn’t use it: a pressed Plain Button scales like every Button. For a pressed state of your own that dims.

tokens.name: opacity-resting
tokens.usage: A chevron at rest: a Disclosure’s, a collapsible Table’s and a SummaryCard’s. A Disclosure’s or a collapsible Table’s rises to full on hover or focus. A `muted-foreground` chevron at it holds 3:1 on every page surface.

tokens.name: opacity-hint
tokens.usage: A table header’s sort arrows before any sort is applied. A `muted-foreground` arrow at it holds 3:1 on `card`.

tokens.name: opacity-pulse
tokens.usage: A skeleton’s faintest point.

motion.note: Durations, easings and a scale. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, a token with a `reducedMotion` value takes it. Components read `duration-standard`, `duration-quick`, `easing-standard` and `easing-spring` through `--ld-dur`, `--ld-dur-quick`, `--ld-ease` and `--ld-spring`, which resolve at `:root`, so set those tokens there.

tokens.name: duration-standard
tokens.usage: Most motion: a press, a disclosure opening, a menu, a switch, a row settling after a swipe.

tokens.name: duration-quick
tokens.usage: Motion in data views, with `easing-standard` so it doesn’t overshoot: a collapsible Table’s chevron turning, a Checkbox filling.

tokens.name: duration-pulse
tokens.usage: Half of a skeleton’s pulse. The pulse is off under reduced motion.

tokens.name: easing-standard
tokens.usage: Decelerates and stops without overshoot: fades, color changes, heights and motion in data views.

tokens.name: easing-spring
tokens.usage: Overshoots a little, then settles: a pressed button, the switch knob, a chevron turning, a row after a swipe.

tokens.name: scale-pressed
tokens.usage: How far a pressed Button shrinks, and the scale a Menu grows from.

layer.note: Stacking of page-level layers. Order inside one component uses 1 to 4 and needs no token.

tokens.name: z-tabbar
tokens.usage: AppShell’s tab bar on narrow screens.

tokens.name: z-selection-bar
tokens.usage: SelectionBar, above the tab bar.

tokens.name: z-glass-bar
tokens.usage: A GlassBar pinned to the top or bottom of the window.

tokens.name: z-menu
tokens.usage: Menus, above every bar.

tokens.name: z-skip-link
tokens.usage: The skip link, above everything while it has focus.

breakpoint.note: Window sizes where layouts change, in em of the browser’s text size, and one container width in px. At the default 16px text an em breakpoint is the px value over 16, so 56.25em is 900px; at 200% text the layout changes at twice the width, as it would on a window half as wide. Media and container queries can’t read custom properties, so these aren’t emitted: registry CSS writes each value. Write an em query in range syntax, `(width < 56.25em)`, in `@media` or `@custom-media`, so a query that stops short of a value needs no 0.02 less. The container width is px because em in `@container` is the container’s font size; a `max-width` query that stops short of it takes 0.02px less.

tokens.name: breakpoint-narrow
tokens.usage: Narrow phones: tab-bar items and the selection bar tighten, and an open message’s padding shrinks.

tokens.name: breakpoint-medium
tokens.usage: StepIndicator lists every step instead of a summary.

tokens.name: breakpoint-sidebar
tokens.usage: AppShell shows its sidebar instead of a tab bar, and summary cards widen.

tokens.name: breakpoint-split
tokens.usage: MasterDetail, WorkbenchShell and an open message go side by side.

tokens.name: breakpoint-short
tokens.usage: A window height. Below it, an open message scrolls with the page instead of inside itself.

tokens.name: breakpoint-card-narrow
tokens.usage: A container width, a DataTable card’s. In a narrower card the status moves under the text.

tokens.name: breakpoint-reflow
tokens.usage: A window under 20em of the browser’s text size: a phone at 200% text, or under 320px at the default size. There a ListRow subtitle wraps, InboxFlow’s preview keeps to one line, WorkbenchShell’s title takes a line of its own when it doesn’t fit beside the brand, a ListGroup’s summary moves under its title when the two don’t fit and SummaryCard’s figure takes `title-1`.
